documents.title: Kennesaw State University Artificial Intelligence Policy
documents.summary: A short institution-wide policy effective May 1, 2026 that sets ethical and security principles for AI-enabled tools, creates an AI Governance Committee to approve tools and maintain a separate Guidance Document, and requires annual AI training. It sets no rules for how students may use AI in coursework.
documents.stance_why: The policy says users 'shall do so ethically, responsibly, and securely' and defers specifics to 'the KSU Institutional Artificial Intelligence Guidance Document'; it states no allow or ban for student coursework, so it delegates.

units.why: The opening sentence binds all internal stakeholders to use AI-enabled tools 'ethically, responsibly, and securely'; a principle-level statement of scope, so P56, actor all, general, must.
units.anchor: shall do so ethically, responsibly, and securely
units.frag_start: All Kennesaw State University internal stakeholders

units.why: Use cases of AI-enabled tools in 'instructional, learning' and other functions 'must be reviewed and approved by the AI Governance Committee before purchase, deployment, or use'; this vets which tools may be used, so P50 (prefer vetted tools).
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P65 with actor admin; coder B coded P50 with actor all. The source sentence is about approving tool use cases before use by stakeholders, not about contracts or data sharing with providers (those are in the next paragraph), so P50 (vetted tools) fits and P65 does not. The requirement binds the stakeholders who seek to use tools, so actor is all. Phase and modality agreed.
units.anchor: must be reviewed and approved by the AI Governance Committee before purchase, deployment, or use

The listed principles are the content of the ethical standards, not a separate rule naming harms, so they stay in this P56 unit (P53 dropped). The 'protect personal and institutional data' clause is a distinct rule and is kept as its own P50 unit.

documents.summary: A university teaching-office page encouraging faculty to publish an AI policy in each syllabus and offering three templates: prohibited, allowed but not required, and required. The allowed and required templates repeat the same warning, responsibility and credit language, which is coded once.

documents.title: CCSE FYE Policies (Academic Misconduct: AI & Cheating)
documents.summary: The first-year programming page of the computing college says all labs, assignments, quizzes and tests must be written without AI, lists AI use as academic misconduct, and bans AI in exams with penalties up to an F. It applies to the FYE course sequence only.

Repeated warning and credit text in the Required syllabus template is skipped as an exact repeat. One UNCOVERED unit: mandatory annual AI training with acknowledgement.
